h: Two Messiahs Bring Salvation and the Soul’s Final Joy

p: שׂוֹשׂ אָשִׂישׂ בַּה׳ וְגוֹמֵר (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, י)
"I will greatly rejoice in Hashem," etc. (Yeshayahu 61:10).
In the Pesikta on this haftarah:
'I will rejoice' — in the days of Mashiach;
'I will greatly rejoice' — at the downfall of the wicked nation;
'my soul shall exult in my God'
this is the war of Gog and Magog."
This refers to the two Mashiachs,
מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד
Mashiach ben Yosef and Mashiach ben David.
through him will come the victory
over the nations of the world,
only at the hand of the children of Rachel,
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז גַּם עַל מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף
which alludes also to Mashiach ben Yosef.
at the downfall of the wicked nation.
And afterward the war of Gog and Magog,
which will be only a remaining existence
of the bad in the nations of the world;
and he will gather the bad
for indeed Gog and Magog has the numerical value seventy;
יִהְיֶה עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד
will be through Mashiach ben David.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר תָּגֵל נַפְשִׁי בֵּאלֹהַי
And of this it says, "My soul shall exult in my God";
for then it will be in the aspect of Shabbos,
דְּאִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רה, א) עַל שַׁבָּת
and not a day of the body."
And of the days of Mashiach
שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לֹא זְכוּת וְלֹא חוֹבָה
in which there is neither merit nor guilt";
for the evil inclination will be nullified.
when there is an evil inclination and free choice;
and then, when the evil inclination is nullified,
מִמֵּילָא יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שַׁבָּת
it will consequently also be like Shabbos,
and this is what is said, "my soul shall exult."
"In six troubles He will save you,
and in seven no harm will touch you."
as they are counted (Vayikra Rabbah, parshah 10):
Egypt, Ashur and the four kingdoms,
and "in seven no harm will touch you"
corresponds to the war of Gog and Magog,
in which in truth there will be no trouble,
"He Who sits in heaven will laugh";
that they will fear that he comes
And corresponding to this the prophet said:
"For He has clothed me in garments of salvation";
this corresponds to Mashiach ben Yosef,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא)
along the lines of what they said (Vayikra Rabbah 21:4):
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה וְעַמֵּךְ כּוּלָּם צַדִּיקִים (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא)
that "your people will all be righteous" (Yeshayahu 60:21),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב כג, א)
and through this will come the victory
for all the subjugation and the exiles
הוּא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם מָקוֹם לְקַטְרֵג
come because they have room to accuse,
some of their bad is found.
"He has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness"
the hei is the middah of Malchus,
the aspect of the Lower Shechinah;
וּמָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת
and Mashiach ben David is a chariot for the middah of Malchus.
And the expression "He has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness"
means that it surrounds from every side,
which is called "the shade of faith,"
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 230a):
And the war of Gog and Magog will be on Sukkos
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב טוּר אוֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן תצ)
and for this reason on Sukkos we read as haftarah
And of Shabbos it is stated (Shabbos 118a–b):
is saved from the subjugation of the kingdoms";
is saved from the war of Gog and Magog";
therefore the consolations are read then,
for on Shabbos one feels the consolations in the heart,
